findings.title: Cached denials can hide newly granted permissions
findings.body: A denial-cache hit returns before checking cached permissions or querying the permission store. If a check is denied and this entry is cached, then the user is granted access to that resource, subsequent checks still deny access until the denial entry expires (30 seconds). This bypasses the new database-refresh path for stale permission-cache misses and can prevent users from accessing newly created resources promptly; invalidate denials when permissions change or otherwise avoid short-circuiting refreshed permissions.

findings.title: Denial-cache key is ambiguous for names containing underscores
findings.body: The name and parent are concatenated with underscores without escaping or length-prefixing, so distinct checks can share a key: for example, name `a_b` with parent `c` collides with name `a` with parent `b_c`. A denial cached for one resource/folder combination then incorrectly denies the other check until expiry. Encode the tuple unambiguously.
